claim: After 28 days of CK21 treatment, no mice from 3 mg/kg or 5 mg/kg groups demonstrated tumor relapse during the subsequent 6-month follow-up observation.

claim: No significant weight loss was detected when female mice were treated with ≤3 mg/kg CK21, compared to the control (no treatment) group.
source: No significant weight loss was detected when female mice were treated with ≤3 mg/kg CK21, compared to the control (no treatment) group (Figure 2d).

claim: Mice exhibited severe weight loss with 5 mg/kg CK21.
source: In contrast, mice exhibited severe weight loss with 5 mg/kg CK21.
evidence: This claim is supported by weight monitoring data.

claim: The kidney, liver, and pancreas tissues appeared normal after 28 days of CK21 treatment at 3 mg/kg.
source: We did not observe any evidence of toxicity, as the kidney, liver, and pancreas tissues appeared normal after 28 days of CK21 treatment (Figure 2e); in contrast, after 14 days of CK21 treatment, AsPC-1 tumors showed a 5-fivefold increase of TUNEL-positive staining compared to the no Rx group (Figure 2f, g).

claim: After 14 days of CK21 treatment, AsPC-1 tumors showed a 5-fold increase of TUNEL-positive staining compared to the no Rx group.
source: We did not observe any evidence of toxicity, as the kidney, liver, and pancreas tissues appeared normal after 28 days of CK21 treatment (Figure 2e); in contrast, after 14 days of CK21 treatment, AsPC-1 tumors showed a 5-fivefold increase of TUNEL-positive staining compared to the no Rx group (Figure 2f, g).

claim: CK21 given at 3 mg/kg daily resulted in significant inhibition of Panc-1 tumor growth.

claim: Orthotopic tumor mouse models are generally preferred over heterotopic subcutaneously located pancreatic tumors because they offer tissue site-specific pathology, allow studies of metastasis, and are deemed more clinically relevant.
source: Orthotopic tumor mouse models are generally preferred over heterotopic subcutaneously located pancreatic tumors because they offer tissue site-specific pathology, allow studies of metastasis, and are deemed more clinically relevant (Qiu and Su, 2013).

claim: The development of pancreatic tumors expressing luciferase/fluorescent proteins has facilitated the longitudinal monitoring of orthotopically located pancreatic tumors.
source: while the development of pancreatic tumors expressing luciferase/fluorescent proteins has facilitated the longitudinal monitoring of orthotopically located pancreatic tumors (Shannon et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shannon et al., 2015.

claim: A 10–15-fold reduction in bioluminescence intensity was observed in mice that received CK21 compared to untreated controls in the orthotopic AsPC-1 model.
source: The presence and size of the tumor were monitored weekly by quantifying the bioluminescence intensity (Figure 2h), and overall, a 10–15-fold reduction in bioluminescence intensity was observed in mice that received CK21 compared to untreated controls (Figure 2i).
evidence: This claim is supported by bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 2h, i.

claim: No mice died in the CK21 treatment group in the orthotopic AsPC-1 model, whereas 5 out of 11 animals were sacrificed in the no Rx group due to the large tumor size.
source: In addition, no mice died in the CK21 treatment group, whereas 5 out of 11 animals were sacrificed in the no Rx group due to the large tumor size (Figure 2j).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival data shown in Figure 2j.

claim: Most of the untreated mice develop metastatic disease by the end of the experiment in the orthotopic AsPC-1 model.

claim: The CK21 treated mice did not develop metastatic disease in the orthotopic AsPC-1 model.
source: Finally, we noted that while most of the untreated mice develop metastatic disease by the end of the experiment (Figure 2h), the CK21 treated mice did not.
evidence: This claim is supported by bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: All mice with orthotopic AsPC-1 tumors relapsed eventually after 4 weeks of CK21 treatment, in contrast to subcutaneous AsPC-1 tumors.
source: After 4 weeks of treatment, mice were monitored up to 3 months. All mice relapsed eventually in contrast to subcutaneous AsPC-1 tumors.
evidence: This claim is supported by long-term follow-up data.

claim: CK21 was able to completely reduce the size of AsPC-1 tumors after 28 days of treatment, even when treatment was initiated after tumors reached a large size of ~900 mm2.
source: To evaluate the efficacy of CK21 against late-stage tumors, CK21 treatment was initiated only after subcutaneous AsPC-1 tumors reached a large size of ~900 mm2 (Figure 3a). Despite this delay in the initiation of treatment, CK21 was able to completely reduce the size of AsPC-1 tumors after 28 days of treatment, with all mice showing a significant response (Figure 3b).
evidence: This claim is supported by delayed treatment tumor growth data shown in Figure 3a, b.

claim: The combination therapy of CK21 and gemcitabine did not show improved inhibition of AsPC-1 growth compared to CK21 monotherapy.
source: The combination therapy did not show improved inhibition of AsPC-1 growth compared to CK21 monotherapy (Figure 3d) and failed to induce complete regression of AsPC-1 tumors.
evidence: This claim is supported by combination therapy tumor growth data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Switching to daily CK21 monotherapy for 28 days induced significant tumor regression in mice where tumors were detectable after 28 days treatment with CK21 or gemcitabine monotherapy, or combination therapy.
source: We observed that irrespective of whether mice failed CK21 (3 x/wk) or gemcitabine monotherapy, or combination therapy, switching to daily CK21 monotherapy for 28 days induced significant tumor regression (Figure 3e).
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue therapy tumor growth data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: 3-D patient-derived organoids offer a better recapitulation of the heterogeneous, architectural, morphologic and genetic features of patient pancreatic tumor, compared to long-term established 2-D monolayer cell lines.
source: It is now recognized that 3-D patient-derived organoids offer a better recapitulation of the heterogeneous, architectural, morphologic and genetic features of patient pancreatic tumor, compared to long-term established 2-D monolayer cell lines (Weeber et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2015; Seino et al., 2018; Boj et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Weeber et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2015; Seino et al., 2018; Boj et al., 2015.

claim: 72 hours of in vitro incubation with CK21 (25 nM) significantly inhibited UC12-0118-8, U049MAI, and U123SOK growth.
source: We observed that 72 hours of in vitro incubation with CK21 (25 nM) significantly inhibited UC12-0118-8, U049MAI, and U123SOK growth, and CK21 (50 nM) significantly inhibited proliferation of all four organoids (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro organoid proliferation assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: CK21 (50 nM) significantly inhibited proliferation of all four organoids (UC12-0118-8, U049MAI, U123SOK, and U123M15-T).
source: We observed that 72 hours of in vitro incubation with CK21 (25 nM) significantly inhibited UC12-0118-8, U049MAI, and U123SOK growth, and CK21 (50 nM) significantly inhibited proliferation of all four organoids (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro organoid proliferation assay data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Treatment with CK21 (3 mg/kg, daily) for 28 days significantly reduced U049MAI tumor growth compared to the untreated control group.
source: In addition, we were able to propagate U049MAI as a slow-growing subcutaneous tumor in nude mice. Treatment with CK21 (3 mg/kg, daily) for 28 days, also significantly reduced U049MAI tumor growth compared to the untreated control group (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo tumor growth data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) significantly increased with prolonged CK21 treatment, from less than 10 DEGs at 3 hr up to 8,000 DEGs at 12 hr.
source: We hypothesized that these early time points might reveal the initiating mechanism of action that result ultimately in the control of tumor growth; indeed, the number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) significantly increased with prolonged CK21 treatment, from less than 10 DEGs at 3 hr up to 8,000 DEGs at 12 hr (Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: CK21 treatment results in significant downregulation of DDIT4, MYC, XBP1 and XIAP.
source: We confirmed with qPCR, of a significant downregulation of DDIT4, MYC, XBP1 and XIAP, as well as a significant upregulation of POLR2A, GADD45 and VAMP1 (Figure 4e).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: CK21 treatment results in significant upregulation of POLR2A, GADD45 and VAMP1.
source: We confirmed with qPCR, of a significant downregulation of DDIT4, MYC, XBP1 and XIAP, as well as a significant upregulation of POLR2A, GADD45 and VAMP1 (Figure 4e).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: CK21 induced similar DEG expression profiles in vivo as in vitro treated organoids, with downregulated DDIT4 and XBP1, as well as upregulated POLR2A.
source: We also performed transcriptome analysis on the AsPC-1 tumor, orthotopically implanted in the pancreas for 7 days and then treated by CK21 for three days. Notably, CK21 induced similar DEG expression profiles as in vitro treated organoids, with downregulated DDIT4 and XBP1, as well as upregulated POLR2A (Figure 4g).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4g.

claim: DDIT4 was one of the genes consistently and strongly downregulated by CK21 in both organoids and AsPC-1, with significant effects observed as early as 3 hours of CK21 treatment in vitro and at day 3 in vivo.
source: DDIT4 was one of the genes consistently and strongly downregulated by CK21 in both organoids and AsPC-1, with significant effects observed as early as 3 hoursr of CK21 treatment in vitro and at day 3 in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq and RT-qPCR data.

claim: DDIT4 has been identified as a prognosis marker and highly expressed in pancreatic tumors.
source: Interestingly, DDIT4 has been identified as a prognosis marker and highly expressed in pancreatic tumors (Pinto et al., 2017), thus prompting the investigation into whether DDIT4 inhibition might be the triggering mechanism of action and thus serve as a predictive biomarker for CK21 sensitivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pinto et al., 2017.

claim: Knock-down of DDIT4 in Panc-1 only induced very modest in vitro susceptibility to CK21.
source: However, knock-down of DDIT4 in Panc-1 only induced very modest in vitro susceptibility to CK21, and the overexpression of DDIT4 in AsPC-1 didn't result a difference to CK21 response (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro proliferation assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Overexpression of DDIT4 in AsPC-1 didn't result in a difference to CK21 response.
source: However, knock-down of DDIT4 in Panc-1 only induced very modest in vitro susceptibility to CK21, and the overexpression of DDIT4 in AsPC-1 didn't result a difference to CK21 response (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro proliferation assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Two mouse pancreatic tumor cell lines derived from genetically modified KC or KPC mice were only modestly sensitive to CK21 treatment.
source: Furthermore, in two mouse pancreatic tumor cell lines derived from genetically modified KC or KPC mice that were only modestly sensitive to CK21 treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), DDIT4 as well as other early responder genes showed strong alterations in expression profiles comparable to tumors that were more sensitive to CK21 (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo tumor growth data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: DDIT4 as well as other early responder genes showed strong alterations in expression profiles in KC or KPC mouse tumors comparable to tumors that were more sensitive to CK21.
source: Furthermore, in two mouse pancreatic tumor cell lines derived from genetically modified KC or KPC mice that were only modestly sensitive to CK21 treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), DDIT4 as well as other early responder genes showed strong alterations in expression profiles comparable to tumors that were more sensitive to CK21 (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: These early responder genes are not likely to be essential mediators leading to tumor susceptibility to CK21.
source: Therefore, these early responder genes are not likely to be essential mediators leading to tumor susceptibility to CK21.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that DDIT4 manipulation did not significantly alter CK21 response.

claim: At the later timepoint of 12 hr after CK21 treatment, both U049MAI and U123M15-T had over 8,000 DEGs compared to the no Rx group.
source: At the later timepoint of 12 hr after CK21 treatment, both U049MAI and U123M15-T had over 8,000 DEGs compared to the no Rx group (Figure 5a, b).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5a, b.

claim: CK21 treatment was predicted to inhibit RNA and DNA transcription, expression of RNA, and transactivation of RNA transcription in both organoids.
source: First, CK21 treatment was predicted to inhibit RNA and DNA transcription, expression of RNA, and transactivation of RNA transcription in both organoids; this observation corroborates a previous report on the ability of triptolide to inhibit RNA transcription (Titov et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis and citation to Titov et al., 2011.

claim: DEGs induced by CK21 were enriched for inhibition of cell proliferation and cell survival, and for inducing apoptosis and tumor cell necrosis.
source: In addition, DEGs induced by CK21 were enriched for inhibition of cell proliferation and cell survival, and for inducing apoptosis and tumor cell necrosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis.

claim: Induction of cell apoptosis is the likely mechanism for the anti-tumor activity of CK21.
source: These observations collectively are consistent with TUNEL-positive staining of ASPC-1 with CK21 treatment in vivo, and support the conclusion that induction of cell apoptosis is the likely mechanism for the anti-tumor activity of CK21.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data from pathway analysis and TUNEL staining.

claim: In both organoids, EIF2 signaling, oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial dysfunction were the major pathways highly upregulated by CK21.
source: Interestingly, in both organoids, EIF2 signaling, oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial dysfunction were the major pathways highly upregulated by CK21, whereas the NF-κB, TGF-ß and telomerase signaling pathways were significantly downregulated at the 12 hr treatment timepoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis.

claim: The NF-κB, TGF-ß and telomerase signaling pathways were significantly downregulated at the 12 hr treatment timepoint in both organoids.
source: Interestingly, in both organoids, EIF2 signaling, oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial dysfunction were the major pathways highly upregulated by CK21, whereas the NF-κB, TGF-ß and telomerase signaling pathways were significantly downregulated at the 12 hr treatment timepoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis.

claim: At 9 hour timepoint, NF-κB was already significantly downregulated and oxidative phosphorylation as well as EIF2 signaling pathway were significantly upregulated.
source: In addition, at 9 hour timepoint, NF-κB was already significantly downregulated and oxidative phosphorylation as well as EIF2 signaling pathway were significantly upregulated (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Aspc-1 orthotopic tumors showed upregulation of DNA damage checkpoint regulation in vivo.
source: In vivo, Aspc-1 orthotopic tumors showed upregulation of DNA damage checkpoint regulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), which also is an indicator of tumor apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: CK21 may be inhibiting NF-κB activity and inducing mitochondrial-mediated tumor cell apoptosis.
source: Collectively, these observations suggest that CK21 may be inhibiting NF-κB activity and inducing mitochondrial-mediated tumor cell apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data from pathway analysis.

claim: NF-κB plays a major role in the regulation of immune, inflammatory response and cell proliferation.
source: NF-κB plays a major role in the regulation of immune, inflammatory response and cell proliferation (Park and Hong, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Park and Hong, 2016.

claim: In tumor cells, particularly in pancreatic cancer cells, NF-κB becomes constitutively activated and has an anti-apoptotic function.
source: In normal cells, NF-κB is activated by appropriate stimuli and then returns to its inactive state. In tumor cells, particularly in pancreatic cancer cells, NF-κB becomes constitutively activated and has an anti-apoptotic function (Liptay et al., 2003; Dolcet et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Liptay et al., 2003; Dolcet et al., 2005.

claim: After 12 hr treatment with CK21, the genes (CHUK, IKBKB and RELA) encoding the key regulators of the NF-κB pathway, IKKα, IKKβ and p65, were significantly downregulated in both organoids.
source: After 12 hr treatment with CK21, the genes (CHUK, IKBKB and RELA) encoding the key regulators of the NF-κB pathway, IKKα, IKKβ and p65, were significantly downregulated in both organoids (Figure 6a).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: After treatment with CK21 for 24 or 48 hours, both AsPC-1 and Panc-1 cell lines exhibited significantly lower expression of p65.
source: After treatment with CK21 for 24 or 48 hours, both cell lines exhibited significantly lower expression of p65, consistent with RNA-seq analysis (Figure 6c).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: CK21 treatment resulted in reduced similarity of p65 and nuclei, indicating significantly reduced translocation of NF-κB to the nuclei.
source: In addition, we observed reduced similarity of p65 and nuclei, indicating significantly reduced translocation of NF-κB to the nuclei in the presence of CK21 (Figure 6d, e).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6d, e.

claim: CK21 inhibits NF-κB expression and translocation, which results in increased susceptibility tumor cell apoptosis.
source: Taken together, the data demonstrate that CK21 inhibits NF-κB expression and translocation, which we hypothesize results in increased susceptibility tumor cell apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data from imaging flow cytometry and pathway analysis.

claim: The expression of genes encoding five mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes were significantly increased in pancreatic tumor organoids treated with CK21.
source: The expression of genes encoding five mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes were significantly increased in pancreatic tumor organoids treated with CK21 (Figure 6f), consistent with dysregulated mitochondrial function and increased susceptibility to mitochondrial-mediated apoptosis (Márquez-Jurado et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: Dysregulated mitochondrial function increases susceptibility to mitochondrial-mediated apoptosis.
source: The expression of genes encoding five mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes were significantly increased in pancreatic tumor organoids treated with CK21 (Figure 6f), consistent with dysregulated mitochondrial function and increased susceptibility to mitochondrial-mediated apoptosis (Márquez-Jurado et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Márquez-Jurado et al., 2018.

claim: A trend towards an increase in ROS was observed as early as 8 hours after CK21 treatment in AsPC-1 and Panc-1.
source: In both cell lines, a trend towards an increase in ROS was observed as early as 8 hours after CK21 treatment, and a significant increase in ROS generation after 24 hours of culture with CK21 (Figure 6g).
evidence: This claim is supported by ROS assay data shown in Figure 6g.

claim: A significant increase in ROS generation was observed after 24 hours of culture with CK21 in AsPC-1 and Panc-1.
source: In both cell lines, a trend towards an increase in ROS was observed as early as 8 hours after CK21 treatment, and a significant increase in ROS generation after 24 hours of culture with CK21 (Figure 6g).
evidence: This claim is supported by ROS assay data shown in Figure 6g.

claim: Increased ROS production may trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and release of pro-apoptotic mitochondrial proteins into the cytoplasm.
source: These observations raise the possibility that increased ROS production may trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and release of pro-apoptotic mitochondrial proteins into the cytoplasm (Márquez-Jurado et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is speculative and supported by citation to Márquez-Jurado et al., 2018.

claim: The B-cell-lymphoma protein 2 (BCL2) family of proteins play critical roles in regulating the mitochondrial pathway of apoptosis.
source: The B-cell-lymphoma protein 2 (BCL2) family of proteins also play critical roles in regulating the mitochondrial pathway of apoptosis, and BCL2 functions as a critical anti-apoptotic survival protein (Redza-Dutordoir and Averill-Bates, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Redza-Dutordoir and Averill-Bates, 2016.

claim: BCL2 functions as a critical anti-apoptotic survival protein.
source: The B-cell-lymphoma protein 2 (BCL2) family of proteins also play critical roles in regulating the mitochondrial pathway of apoptosis, and BCL2 functions as a critical anti-apoptotic survival protein (Redza-Dutordoir and Averill-Bates, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Redza-Dutordoir and Averill-Bates, 2016.

claim: BCL2 was significantly decreased in both AsPC-1 and Panc-1 cell lines, and in U049MAI, after 24 hours of CK21 culture.
source: We observed that BCL2 was significant decreased in both AsPC-1 and Panc-1 cell lines, and in U049MAI, after 24 hours of CK21 culture (Figure 6h).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6h.

claim: Most apoptotic pathways lead to the activation of cysteine-dependent aspartate-specific proteases, and ultimately to cleaved effector caspases such as caspases-3,–6 and –7.
source: Because most apoptotic pathways lead to the activation of cysteine-dependent aspartate-specific proteases, and ultimately to cleaved effector caspases such as caspases-3,–6 and –7 Redza-Dutordoir and Averill-Bates, 2016, we probed for cleaved caspase-3 in pancreatic tumors incubated with CK21.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Redza-Dutordoir and Averill-Bates, 2016.

claim: For Panc-1 and both pancreatic tumor organoids, cleaved caspase-3 was detected after 24 hours of culture with CK21.
source: For Panc-1 and both pancreatic tumor organoids, cleaved caspase-3 was detected after 24 hours of culture with CK21 (Figure 6i) by Western blotting.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6i.

claim: Increased caspase-3/7 in Panc-1 was confirmed by flow cytometry.
source: We also confirmed increased caspase-3/7 in Panc-1 by flow cytometry (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cleaved caspase-3/7 was not detected in AsPC-1 after CK21 treatment.
source: Interesting, cleaved caspase-3/7 was not detected in AsPC-1 after CK21 treatment, suggesting that apoptosis of these tumor cells may be explained by the involvement of other effector caspases or proteases.

claim: Apoptosis of AsPC-1 tumor cells may be explained by the involvement of other effector caspases or proteases.
source: Interesting, cleaved caspase-3/7 was not detected in AsPC-1 after CK21 treatment, suggesting that apoptosis of these tumor cells may be explained by the involvement of other effector caspases or proteases.
evidence: This claim is speculative and inferred from the absence of cleaved caspase-3/7 in AsPC-1.

claim: CK21 downregulates the NF-kB pathway, promotes ROS production and mitochondrial-mediated tumor cell apoptosis.
source: Collectively, these data point to CK21 downregulating the NF-kB pathway, promoting ROS production and mitochondrial-mediated tumor cell apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data from pathway analysis, ROS assays, and apoptosis assays.

claim: A number of studies have reported on the immunosuppressive activity of triptolide.
source: A number of studies have reported on the immunosuppressive activity of triptolide (Chen, 2001), thus raising the potential concern that CK21 may also inhibit the development of anti-tumor immune responses and prevent long-term tumor control.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Chen, 2001.

claim: IPA analysis indicated that CK21 inhibited lymphopoiesis, leukopoiesis and T cell development.
source: Indeed, although the analyses were conducted on CK21 treated tumor cells, IPA analysis indicated that CK21 inhibited lymphopoiesis, leukopoiesis and T cell development, consistent with potential immunosuppressive activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis.

claim: Upon subcutaneous implantation into B6.129 immunocompetent hosts, KPC-960 grew to a maximum tumor size by day 7 and then approximately 70% KPC-960 tumors were spontaneously rejected by day 14–17 post-implantation.
source: Upon subcutaneous implantation into B6.129 immunocompetent hosts, KPC-960 grew to a maximum tumor size by day 7 and then approximately 70% KPC-960 tumors were spontaneously rejected by day 14–17 post-implantation (Figure 7b).
evidence: This claim is supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 7b.

claim: No statistically significant inhibition of tumor regression was observed when CK21 treatment was started on day 5 or 7 post-implantation of KPC-960.
source: We observed no statistically significant inhibition of tumor regression when CK21 treatment was started on day 5 or 7 post-implantation (Figure 7c, d) suggesting that the immunosuppressive activity of CK21 on established primary immune responses is minimal.
evidence: This claim is supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 7c, d.

claim: The immunosuppressive activity of CK21 on established primary immune responses is minimal.
source: We observed no statistically significant inhibition of tumor regression when CK21 treatment was started on day 5 or 7 post-implantation (Figure 7c, d) suggesting that the immunosuppressive activity of CK21 on established primary immune responses is minimal.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that CK21 did not inhibit tumor rejection.

claim: KPC-960 showed limited efficacy to CK21 when implanted subcutaneously into nude mice at 3 mg/kg/day.
source: We also implanted KPC-960 subcutaneously into nude mice but observed limited efficacy by CK21 when provided at 3 mg/kg/day (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Host immunity is primary responsible for the rejection of KPC-960 tumors.
source: These observations suggest that host immunity is primary responsible for the rejection of KPC-960 tumors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that KPC-960 is rejected in immunocompetent mice but not in nude mice.

claim: Mice that cleared KPC-960 tumors while receiving CK21 were able to reject a second KPC-960 tumor comparably to those that did not receive CK21.
source: In addition, mice that rejected the first KPC-960 tumors while receiving CK21 were rested and re-challenged with a second KPC-960 tumor. All the mice were able to reject the tumor comparably to those that did not receive CK21, (Figure 7g).
evidence: This claim is supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 7g.

claim: CK21 did not inhibit the development of memory or recall anti-tumor responses.
source: These observations further demonstrate CK21 did not inhibit the development of memory or recall anti-tumor responses.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that mice treated with CK21 could reject a second tumor challenge.

claim: Splenocytes from mice treated with CK21 exhibited comparable killing of KPC-960 as splenocytes from untreated mice.
source: Splenocytes from mice treated with CK21 exhibited comparable killing of KPC-960 as splenocytes from untreated mice (Figure 7i).
evidence: This claim is supported by ex vivo tumor killing assay data shown in Figure 7i.

claim: Despite potent anti-tumor activity, CK21 was minimally immunosuppressive.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that despite potent anti-tumor activity, CK21 was minimally immunosuppressive.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined data from tumor rejection studies and ex vivo killing assays.

claim: Hepatotoxicity, reproductive toxicity, and nephrotoxicity have been identified as the major side effects for triptolide.
source: Toxicity is the key challenge for using triptolide and its derivatives as anti-tumor agents in the clinic. Hepatotoxicity, reproductive toxicity, and nephrotoxicity have been identified as the major side effects for triptolide (Li et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Li et al., 2014a.

claim: Sex differences have been observed for triptolide, where the female rats showed more toxicity under the same dosage of triptolide.
source: In addition, sex differences have been observed, where the female rats showed more toxicity under the same dosage of triptolide (Liu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Liu et al., 2010.

claim: Cytochrome P450s (CYP) is essential for the metabolism of triptolide and CYP3A2, a male-predominant form in rats, may contribute to the sex-related differences.
source: Cytochrome P450s (CYP) is essential for the metabolism of triptolide and CYP3A2, a male-predominant form in rats, may contribute to the sex-related differences (Xue et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Xue et al., 2011.

claim: Similar sex differences were observed for CK21, where half the dose of CK21 in female rats had a similar triptolide exposure in plasma as male rats.
source: Similar sex differences were also observed for CK21, where half the dose of CK21 in female rats had a similar triptolide exposure in plasma as male rats (Figure 1e), and the maximum tolerated dose of CK21 was 3 mg/kg/dose for female rats and 6 mg/kg/dose for male rats (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacokinetic data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Stable exposure of triptolide upon conversion from CK21 resulted in significantly mitigated toxicity, compared to other analogs such as F60008 that showed a steep release of triptolide.
source: Nevertheless, despite sex difference, stable exposure of triptolide upon conversion from CK21 resulted in significantly mitigated toxicity, ompared to other analogs such as F60008 that showed a steep release of triptolide which, we speculate, would lead to triptolide overexposure and severe toxicity observed in Phase 1 trials (Kitzen et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is speculative and supported by comparison with F60008 and citation to Kitzen et al., 2009.

claim: MRx102 had a MTD of 3 mg/kg/dose for the female rats and 4.5 mg/kg/dose for the male rats.
source: Another triptolide analog, MRx102 had a MTD of 3 mg/kg/dose for the female rats and 4.5 mg/kg/dose for the male rats (Fidler et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Fidler et al., 2014.

claim: Under the pharmacokinetic profile of CK21, female athymic nude mice could be dosed up to 5 mg/kg/day for 28 days with tolerable weight loss.
source: Thus, under the pharmacokinetic profile of CK21, we were able to dose the female athymic nude mice up to 5 mg/kg/day for 28 days with tolerable weight loss (Figure 2d), and at 3 mg/kg/day, where CK21 showed potent efficacy and no obvious toxicity (Figure 2c–e).
